text:
Lynn Conway was born on January 2, 1938, and raised as a boy, experiencing gender dysphoria, which led to her withdrawing from MIT in 1959 before eventually detransitioning. After working as an electronics technician, she earned her B.S. and M.S.E.E. degrees from Columbia University in 1962 and 1963, respectively.
In 1964, Conway joined IBM Research and worked on the Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) project, contributing to the invention of multiple-issue out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling. After being fired by IBM in 1968 upon revealing her intention to transition, she completed her gender transition in that year, adopted a new name and identity, and began her post-transition career. At Xerox PARC in 1973, she led the "LSI Systems" group, where she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* with Carver Mead. Her key contributions included founding the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology and co-inventing dimensionless, scalable design rules, which helped institutionalize the Metal Oxide Semiconductor Implementation Service (MOSIS) system. She later joined DARPA in 1983 and became a professor at the University of Michigan in 1985.
